transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Quasar CTO), Marcus Lee (Sr Platform Eng), Rina Gupta (ML Eng)

Summary (auto): Discovery call to understand QuasarCommerce integration patterns, decision criteria for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, SDK usage (Python/Node), connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex, network topology (gateway/proxy), rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks for ops.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood. We got Maya, our solutions engineer on the line. Quick round of intros?
00:08 Lena: Hi, Lena here, CTO at QuasarCommerce. Marcus and Rina are my engineers. We're evaluating options to power product search and recommendations with an LLM.
00:15 Maya: Great, hi all. We'll walk through integration patterns and ops concerns - SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex compat, gateway/proxy, rate-limits, observability.
00:30 Marcus: High level - we currently run a microservices stack on EKS, internal API gateway (Kong). Most traffic is read-heavy, peak 1200 reqs/s but LLM features will be smaller subset, maybe 50-150 rps for recommendations. Latency target is 150-250ms p95 for inference.
00:55 Rina: Also important - data residency and PII controls. We can't send raw customer personal data to a public endpoint without controls. SOC2, encryption at rest and in-flight, KMS integration are must-haves.
01:20 Samir: Totally. For that reason many customers evaluate Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Quick mapping: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and per-token pricing, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) lets you run a customer-managed control plane with KMS/HSM and network isolation.
01:45 Lena: If we start hosted for dev, is it easy to move to Dedicated later without rewriting code?
01:52 Maya: Yes. Same API surface. You can pin model versions and adjust routing policies without changing SDK calls. We provide SDKs (Python/Node), REST, and gRPC endpoints; switching is mainly config in your deployment.
02:10 Marcus: Can you show examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex? We use LangChain in a couple services and LlamaIndex in our retrieval pipeline.
02:20 Maya: Sure. We have sample repos. For LangChain you can use our LLM wrapper with the standard Chain interface - basically swap the provider URL and API key. For LlamaIndex, we provide a connector that streams tokens and supports chunked embeddings. I'll share the repo after the call.
02:42 Rina: How's streaming handled? We need partial responses to show in UI and also want the ability to stop generation early if latency spikes.
02:50 Maya: We support server-sent events and websocket streaming. You can stop a stream client-side; on the backend we do graceful cancellation and KV cache management to keep costs low.
03:10 Marcus: Important - we use an internal gateway, so we prefer to route all outbound LLM calls through our proxy for auditing and routing. Can Redwood be called through a gateway/proxy?
03:20 Samir: Yes. Customers commonly use an internal gateway. For Hosted, you'd set the gateway to forward to Redwood endpoint. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your VPC/NAT - we also support private peering in some regions. There are TTL and keepalive knobs the SE can help with.
03:45 Lena: Rate limits and quotas - we have bursty traffic on Black Friday-style events. Can Dedicated scale? And what does throttling look like on Hosted?
03:55 Maya: Dedicated is configurable with autoscaling policies and burst capacity; we size the pool to meet your SLO. Hosted has per-account quotas and rate-limits, and we can offer higher tiers for enterprise customers; if you hit limits we can setup a secondary routing to a cheaper model to avoid hard failures.
04:20 Marcus: Do you expose per-route metrics? We need token-level cost breakdown and per-endpoint latency for our billing and SLO tracking.
04:28 Maya: Yes - Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, token cost breakdown, traces, and tracing hooks that can emit events to your observability stack (Datadog, Cortex, Prometheus). We also support a webhook for usage events.
04:48 Rina: Regarding embeddings - we use the vectors in our search index (we use an in-house vector DB). What's the embedding throughput and batching behavior?
04:55 Maya: We offer an embeddings endpoint with batching and auto-batching. You can set batch size and timeout; we also recommend prefix caching for common contexts. For high throughput, Dedicated with optimized kernels and quantized models reduces per-token cost.
05:20 Marcus: On security - KMS, audit logs, and SSO. We use Okta. Can we integrate with SAML/SSO and have audit events forwarded?
05:28 Samir: Yes, we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. For Hosted we provide audit logs with configurable retention, and you can push them to your SIEM. For Private, logs stay in your control plane. KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) are supported for Dedicated/Private.
05:50 Lena: Any gotchas for LlamaIndex (on-prem index + Redwood hosted)? We worry about sending indexes or chunks with PII.
06:00 Maya: You can use embeddings-only workflows where you tokenize locally and only send non-PII embeddings, or run Redwood Private to keep control. We also offer field-level redaction helpers in the SDK.
06:20 Marcus: Let's talk about cost controls. Can we set per-route budgets or hard quotas per team?
06:29 Maya: Yep - Redwood Console supports per-route/model quotas, token budgets, and alerts. You can enforce a hard cap to reject requests when exceeded, or soft cap to throttle. Also rate-limiter headers are returned so your gateway can route gracefully.
06:50 Rina: Observability hooks - is there an SDK-level hook to emit trace/span IDs? We want to correlate LLM calls with our distributed traces.
06:58 Maya: We add trace headers automatically if you propagate them; otherwise SDKs can accept a trace_id param. We also export spans to OTLP/Datadog if you opt-in.
07:20 Marcus: For the pilot we want to run a benchmark between Hosted and Dedicated to see p95 and cost per 1k requests. What data do you need from us?
07:27 Maya: We'll need your request size distribution (tokens in/prompt length), concurrency targets, and sample prompts. Also whether you need streaming or sync responses. If you send a 7-day traffic profile that's ideal.
07:40 Marcus: We can export that. We'll also want a test harness - can Redwood run a sample load test or provide a harness?
07:48 Samir: We can provide a simple load harness and scripts, and our SEs will help set up the pilot. For Dedicated we'll size a 4xA100 equivalent pool for the pilot and show throughput/latency.
08:05 Lena: How are model updates handled? We want consistent output during canary rollouts.
08:12 Maya: Rollouts are handled via model version pinning and canary rules. You can route a percentage of traffic to a variant and use quality monitoring tied to eval sets - if regression happens we auto-fallback.
08:30 Rina: One operational ask - we want to log model inputs/outputs for debugging, but keep PII redacted. Can Redwood support configurable redaction and separate storage for logs?
08:40 Samir: Yes. You can configure what fields to redact and where logs are stored. For Hosted we can redact before storing; for Dedicated/Private you have full control.
08:58 Marcus: Latency numbers - what p95 can we expect for a 1k token response on an NVL-type model?
09:05 Maya: For a modern quantized model on Dedicated, p95 for 1k tokens depends a lot on batching. At low concurrency you might see 200-400ms per-token overhead; realistically p95 could be 700-1200ms for 1k tokens depending on model and hardware. For many retrieval/qa cases you aim for shorter completions. We can benchmark your real prompts.
09:40 Lena: About integration - what's required to get started for dev team?
09:46 Samir: Sign up for Hosted API, get API key, use SDK, try sample repo (LangChain/LlamaIndex). If you want Dedicated evaluation, we'll propose sizing and a contract for a short pilot period.
10:02 Rina: Any prebuilt connectors to our vector DB? We use Milvus.
10:08 Maya: We have community connectors; SE can share a Milvus integration pattern for embedding pipelines.
10:20 Marcus: Network - if we go Dedicated in a cloud region, can traffic stay within our VPC?
10:26 Maya: For Dedicated we offer private peering and VPC endpoints in supported regions. Private deployment gives full control.
10:35 Marcus: How does rate-limiting manifest at the SDK level? Does SDK surface 429s with retry-after?
10:42 Maya: Yes, SDK surfaces 429 with a retry-after header and provides client-side rate limit helpers; we also return granular headers for token usage so your gateway can make decisions.
10:55 Lena: Any enterprise security artifacts you can send? We'll want SOC2, ISO if available, and pen test summary.
11:02 Samir: I'll send SOC2 and our security FAQ. We also have an architecture doc for Dedicated/Private.
11:10 Marcus: For the pilot, are there limits on model choice? Like can we use open models or do you have Redwood-verified models?
11:18 Maya: We support a catalog of curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. You can bring your own model for Private, and for Dedicated we can onboard open weights; some models might need quantization work.
11:38 Rina: About caching - how does KV cache work with streaming and partial responses?
11:45 Maya: KV cache is per-session and stores key/value states for autoregressive decoding. With streaming we flush partial tokens but maintain cache entries; it's mostly transparent. For retrieval-augmented flows we recommend prefix caching for repeated contexts.
12:00 Samir: Quick recap and proposed next steps?
12:05 Lena: We'd like pricing for Dedicated pilot, SOC2/security docs, and LangChain/LlamaIndex sample integration. Also a date for pilot bench week of 2027-04-18.
12:18 Samir: Got it. We'll send pricing + SOC2 by 4/10, Maya will share samples by 4/12, and Marcus will share traffic profile by 4/11. We'll set up a 1-hour kickoff for the pilot next Wednesday - I'll follow up with a calendar invite.
12:40 Marcus: One final question - if we run into a regression after a model update, what's rollback speed?
12:46 Maya: Rollback is essentially instant at routing level - fallback to the previous pinned model. Monitoring detects regressions via eval prompts and we can auto-fallback within minutes.
12:58 Lena: Thanks, that's helpful. We'll review and get the data to you.
13:05 Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll send follow-ups.
